chunks.rationale: test/provenance.test.ts is the contract: it pins what counts as grounding (repo tool calls, memory tools, gh/#refs), the turn boundary, and the chatter threshold. Read it before the classifier so the regexes in src/provenance.ts have a spec to be checked against. The new block in test/threadView.test.tsx (describe 'ThreadView provenance tiers') then proves the strip actually renders in the transcript — the file's own header explains why render coverage matters here.
risks: The 'turn boundary' test only proves scanning stops at a user message; it does not cover event messages interleaved with tool calls (they are skipped, which is intended).
Render tests assert data-tier attributes, not visual placement of the strip above the meta footer.

chunks.rationale: src/provenance.ts is the pure classifier — start at messageProvenance (bottom), then classifyTool/classifyText. Then the ThreadView.tsx diff in render order: provenanceById memo (computes per assistant message over raw detail.messages), the provenance prop passed at the MessageBlock call site, and the ProvenanceStrip component above MessageBlock. Finish with the .provStrip/.provChip rules in ThreadView.module.css.
risks: Evidence is turn-scoped: a long final summary whose reads happened in an earlier turn of the same run shows 'model prior knowledge' even though the run did touch the repo. Deliberate (per-turn attribution), but it is the most likely false-positive a user will report.
Backticked spans that merely look like paths (e.g. `node_modules/foo/index.js`) ground a message the model may never have read — the repo chip asserts citation, not verification against the worktree.
provenanceById recomputes over every assistant message on each detail update (stream tick); regex cost is small but the memo key is the whole detail object.
Truncated tool input falls back to a regex that stops at the first quote — an escaped quote in a path would misparse (cosmetic only, chip label).
Issue refs are collected from gh commands and #-refs without checking the issue exists; chips are labels, not verified links (no click-through in v1).

chunks.rationale: Contract first. electron/test/pr-size-cap.test.js is the guardrail contract: default 400 cap, over-cap refusal BEFORE push/gh (asserts zero 'pr create' calls and no persisted prNumber), allowOversize override, null disables, custom cap, parseNumstat (binary files count as files, not lines). test/planboard.test.ts pins reviewLoad thresholds (busy at 4 PRs / >1200 lines, overloaded at 7 / >2400) and the draft/merged exclusions. test/planboardView.test.tsx proves the meter renders only when listPrs is wired and survives a PR-list failure. test/nextGitActionButton.test.tsx walks the full refusal UI: bar appears, Split sends the restack prompt, Create anyway retries with allowOversize:true, non-cap errors never show the bar. test/prUi.test.ts pins the cross-process message prefix.
risks: The oversize-bar test relies on gitSyncInfo {hasUpstream:true,ahead:0} resolving to the create-pr action; a nextGitAction table change would reroute the test, not break it — the assertions are on the bar, not the action.
pr-size-cap.test.js counts exact lines (450 > 400, 20 > 10); the numstat line count is git-version independent but the assertion strings embed them.

chunks.rationale: electron/worktrees.js: diffStatVsBase (three-dot numstat vs base, fails OPEN — a stat hiccup never blocks a PR) and the cap check inside createPr placed after the ahead-check but BEFORE push, so a refused PR leaves no remote branch and no gh trace. The error message prefix 'PR too large:' is a cross-process contract duplicated in src/prUi.ts (PR_TOO_LARGE_PREFIX) — the two processes share no module. electron/store.js owns the default: absent/junk heals to 400, only explicit null disables (DORA small batches as the shipped default).
risks: createPr is also called by agents via MCP/IPC, not just the header button; the cap applies there too, and the agent only sees the message text. The message must stay self-explanatory.

The cap counts lines vs the project checkout's current branch (defaultBranchAsync), same base the PR would get — but a thread stacked on another branch (#187/#240 not shipped) would be measured against main, overcounting. Accepted until base-branch support lands.
Binary files add 0 lines; a PR of only binary assets never trips the cap. Deliberate.

chunks.rationale: Renderer flow: ThreadView's NextGitActionButton catches the refusal by prefix and swaps in an inline bar (Split into stacked PRs → splitPrPrompt via onStartRun; Create anyway → onCreatePr with allowOversize; dismiss ×). useCoder/ipc.js/preload thread allowOversize through unchanged. Planboard meter: planboard.ts reviewLoad/formatLineCount are pure; PlanboardView fetches listPrs alongside listIssues (Promise.all, stale-gen guard shared), meter sits in the existing header with ok/busy/overloaded colors; App.tsx wires the already-exposed listPrs. SettingsModal gains a 'Pull requests' section with the cap input following the dailyBudgetUsd blur-save pattern; devCoder mirrors the new setting so the web dev build typechecks.
risks: The oversize bar renders as a sibling of the header button inside a flex header; very long messages are ellipsis-clamped (max-width 520px) — full text only in the runError banner is NOT shown for cap refusals (the catch swallows it into the bar), so the bar text is the only copy. It contains lines, base, files, and cap.
reviewLoad thresholds are compile-time constants, not derived from the user's configured cap; a user who raises the cap to 2000 still gets busy at 1200 lines of queue. Kept simple deliberately.

SettingsModal save() now sends prDiffCapLines in the same patch as budgets; backends older than this change would ignore the unknown key (store.setSettings patches per-key) — forward compatible, but a downgraded main process silently drops the cap.

chunks.rationale: test/sidebar.test.tsx new describe block pins the intended behavior first: running subagents nest under the parent card, done/failed render nothing, row click selects the parent thread. Read this to see the contract before the implementation.
risks: Tests only cover the attention list, not the archived-expanded list which got the same Fragment wrap.

chunks.rationale: src/components/Sidebar.tsx: new SubagentRows component (after SelectOpts) filters thread.subagents to status==='running' and renders compact rows that call onSelect(parentId). Both ThreadCard map sites (attention ~2926, archived ~2985) are wrapped in a Fragment keyed `${id}:card` to preserve the t3 unmount/remount key rule documented above the attention map.
risks: SubagentRows is not memoized; it re-renders with each sidebar tick. It is tiny (filter + map over <=20 rows) and only mounts rows while subagents run, so cost is negligible.
Shift-click on a subagent row forwards shift to onSelect, which may range-select threads; same semantics as clicking the parent card, judged harmless.

chunks.rationale: src/components/Sidebar.module.css: .subagentList/.subagentRow reuse the nested-card geometry (width calc(100% - 14px), margin-left 14px, ::before elbow at left -9px) so subagent rows align exactly with nested worker cards; the pulsing dot reuses the existing .waitingDot class/animation from the wait line.
risks: Elbow is per-row (top -4px to 50%), so multiple rows draw a chain of elbows rather than one continuous spine; matches how consecutive nested worker cards already look.

Running-only is a deliberate scope cut (issue #542): finished subagents remain visible in the Agents panel Subagents section, not the sidebar. If the user expected done rows too, this is the line to revisit.

chunks.rationale: Contract first: electron/test/quota-wait.test.js is the parser (Claude/Codex/Kimi clocks, ISO/duration/Retry-After, #286 exclusion, wake-once, opt-out). electron/test/quota-wait-runner.test.js is the live runner (park, no-clock fail, budget fail, global opt-out, wake-once without a second user message, resumeQuotaWait). Renderer: test/quotaWait.test.ts, sidebarFailedBadge, settingsModal, kanban, threadSettle. Ask-mode suites must still pass — startAskRun shares fromQuotaWait and markRunFailed.

Issue #401 felt-vs-actual: the new tests state the contract before the code does — test/fleet.test.ts (perception rollup), electron/test/felt-estimate.test.js (service + migration), electron/test/fleet.test.js (collector carries feltSavedMs), test/feltCard.test.tsx (one-tap card), test/fleetView.test.tsx (felt vs actual section).
risks: fleetView threadRow/summary factories gained required fields; any other hand-built FleetSummary/FleetThreadRow literal in the suite would fail at runtime, not compile time (strip-types).

chunks.rationale: src/shared/ipc.ts is the contract everything else mirrors: FeltEstimate type, FELT_ESTIMATE_BUCKETS_MS/MAX, ThreadInfo.feltEstimate (optional so legacy fixtures still typecheck), FleetThread.feltSavedMs (required — evidence is always rebuilt), threads.setFeltEstimate in CoderApi. Then electron/services.js setFeltEstimate (validation, clamp, decline, no updatedAt bump) and electron/store.js normalizeFeltEstimate/migrateThread.
risks: FELT_ESTIMATE_MAX_MS is mirrored by hand between ipc.ts and services.js (CJS cannot import the TS constant) — they must stay in sync.
updateThread is called without touch, matching setNotes; adding touch later would corrupt the sidebar age label and fleet endedAt.

chunks.rationale: Read in data-flow order: electron/fleet.js feltSavedMsOf + row field → src/fleet.ts readThread/FleetPerception/perception sums → src/components/ThreadView.tsx FeltEstimateCard (render gate: status done, no estimate, not ask/teach) → src/components/FleetView.tsx perception section + per-thread Felt column → wiring (useCoder.setFeltEstimate, App handler, preload, wireClient, fakeCoder, devCoder fixtures).
risks: The card appears on every done thread lacking an estimate, including very old ones after upgrade — first open of an ancient thread will show the card once; Skip dismisses permanently. Deliberate, but noticeable.
FeltEstimateCard reads FELT_ESTIMATE_BUCKETS_MS by index into FELT_BUCKET_LABELS; adding a bucket without a label would render undefined.
Perception ratios divide felt by wall/active of ONLY the estimated threads, not all threads — mixing denominators would bias the gap.

chunks.rationale: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md fleet section gained a 'Felt vs actual' subsection so the two-halves-meet-in-the-rollup design is discoverable.

risks: Feature is display-only: chips have titles but no click-through to file/memory/issue, although the issue calls those tiers 'addressable'. Addressability is a follow-up.
PRIOR_MIN_CHARS=240 is a judgement call; recaps just under the threshold escape the prior tag.

Auto-split is agent-mediated (splitPrPrompt restacks the branch), not a git-level splitter: true stacked-PR UX (position badges, safe-prefix merge) remains #240. The prompt instructs --base <previous-slice-branch> so the chain is correct even before #240 ships.
The review-load meter reads gh pr list additions/deletions; on old gh versions listPrs falls back to the short field set and lines show as 0 — the meter then reflects PR count only.
fleet.js already aggregates similar PR data; the meter deliberately reuses listPrs instead to stay per-project and failure-in-band. If a third consumer appears, unify.

No dedicated ThreadInfo.endedAt exists; fleet wall clock uses updatedAt, so a felt estimate recorded long after activity still compares against last-activity time — honest but worth knowing when reading the ratio.
Electron suite had 7 pre-existing failures on main (tracked #536); verify this branch's failures do not exceed that baseline.
Agents panel needed no change: the Subagents section (AgentsPanel.tsx ~2373) already renders subagents with TeamRow visuals in all non-workflow branches.
No electron/runner changes: subagent detection (runner.js addSubagentRow) and ThreadInfo.subagents transport already existed and feed the sidebar threads list.
This is a resurrection of 688e5a9 after 8bf223b deleted the feature in Ask-mode conflict resolution. Both features must stay. Do not drop fromQuotaWait on startAskRun.
Distinct from #286 (Solenta budget) and #294 (model failover). Exhausted balance with no reset clock fails once.
No MCP spec_dispatch/spec_converge tools — agents on the spec thread cannot trigger these without the card. Deliberate: issue asked for IPC + spec card, same seam as startSpec/reviewSpec.
No runner hook to dispatch the next wave when the last worker of the current wave completes.

The state-change pin effect is unchanged. This only covers post-paint growth (images, highlight, webfonts). A reviewer who deletes the new effect and keeps the old one would still have a green suite except the two #408 tests.
Issue #184 asked for a protocolVersion handshake. That was deliberately replaced with SHA equality and is NOT reintroduced here — only the hard-stop UX gap is closed.
